claim: lagged occupancy effects disappear after static spatial control
literature_hit: Autocovariate vs spatially-correlated random effects disentangling in binary SDMs
reference: Crase/Thomas et al. 2020, Ecology 101 (Disentangling drivers of spatial autocorrelation in SDMs); Dormann 2007 autologistic critique
overlap: strong conceptual precedent (spatial autocovariate vs static random effect)
our_difference: temporal lag rather than contemporaneous neighbour autocovariate; prospective forward-chaining validation; 116-species continental scale; occupancy vs abundance contrast
novelty_status: partially novel — cite and reposition as temporal analogue

claim: dynamic occupancy models improve range predictions
literature_hit: Dynocc models with habitat vs connectivity terms, 46 Catalan birds
reference: Ecography 2024 (ecog.06985); Altwegg et al.; Tavecchia et al. Swiss birds GCB 2022
overlap: uses lagged occupancy + habitat; finds modest gains from explicit dynamics
our_difference: we decompose the *lagged-state signal itself* into static vs temporal components rather than comparing model classes

claim: apparent ecological memory is spatial heterogeneity
literature_hit: Space-for-time substitution decomposition of climate effects on bird abundance
reference: Bosch et al. 2022 GCB (Fennoscandian birds; spatial/temporal/spatiotemporal climate components)
overlap: decomposes environmental effects into spatial vs temporal for 39 mountain birds
our_difference: our decomposition is of lagged-state predictability, not climate; forward-chaining + route demeaning; occupancy/abundance divergence
novelty_status: partially novel — same decomposition philosophy, different object

claim: occupancy and abundance history effects diverge across many species
literature_hit: Temporal occupancy vs spatial occupancy vs abundance, NEON small mammals
reference: Holian et al. 2026 Ecol Evol ece3.73214
overlap: links temporal persistence to abundance at site level
our_difference: we directly contrast matched-environment occupancy hysteresis (null) vs abundance prior-state effect (strong) within the same species and design
novelty_status: novel — no direct prior test found

claim: prospective forward validation changes lag-state interpretation
literature_hit: Space-time dynamic occupancy forecasting from BBS (USGS/Clement et al.)
reference: USGS EESC program; Clement et al. 2016 GCB
overlap: dynamic occupancy forecasts from BBS exist
our_difference: we use forward-chaining specifically as a *diagnostic* to separate prospective signal from retrospective fit, not as a forecasting product
novelty_status: novel usage of a standard design

our_difference: we quantify it under matched environment and forward-chaining across 116 species and contrast with occupancy
novelty_status: confirmatory by design — framed as contrast, not discovery
